notes: Direct HTTP fetch worked throughout, no blocks. Checked main nav (104 unique /collections/ links from homepage -- none named clearance/outlet/final-sale/last-chance/end-of-line), footer, and sitemap_collections_1.xml (308 handles grepped for clearance|outlet|final-sale|last-chance|end-of-line|discontinued|sale) -- no clearance/outlet-named collection exists anywhere on the site; full-text search of fetched homepage HTML for 'clearance','outlet','final sale','last chance','end of line','discontinued' = zero hits. Site's own search (/search?q=...) was also checked as supporting evidence: confirmed the search engine is discriminating, not a flat default-for-everything responder (a nonsense query 'zzzxxxqqqnonsense' returned '0 results'), so a query result is meaningful. 'clearance' returned '330 results' and 'outlet' returned '56 results', but inspecting the actual result titles showed unrelated products (whiskey glass set, textured cushion, soap bar) -- i.e. loose/fuzzy text-matching artifacts, not a dedicated clearance/outlet PLP; this is a true absence, not a search-is-non-discriminating false negative. The only discount-style collections found (via sitemap) are five generic percentage-off tiers: /collections/sale-20, sale-30, sale-40, sale-50, sale-60 (titles/H1s literally 'Sale 20%'...'Sale 60%'; qty 122/73/48/51/25 respectively via products.json unique-id enumeration). Per brief S3 Sale-vs-Clearance test these were evaluated and excluded: no permanence signal anywhere on the site (no 'final sale'/'last chance'/'end of line'/'outlet' wording in nav, footer, or page content) -- they read as temporary percent-off promotional tiers, which the brief explicitly instructs NOT to include as Clearance ('a percent-off campaign with no permanence signal' is the brief's own example of the exclude case, not an ambiguous one). No genuine Clearance PLP exists on this site.
